questions.knowledge_point: Inverting Affine Transformations Given in Matrix Form
questions.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find $a+b+c,$ given that the matrix form of the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ a & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $T$ gives us the following information:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-9 & 2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-1\cdot (-9)-2\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-4+(-9)+20=7.
$$

questions.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -9 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find $a+b+c,$ given that the matrix form of the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & -3 \\ 1 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $T$ gives us the following information:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-5 & -9 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6\cdot (-5)-(-9)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ -3 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ -3 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-2+\frac{5}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=0.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Inverting Affine Transformations Given in Parametric Form
questions.problem:
The affine transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2u-v+1,\,y=9u-4v+3.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ of $T$ is

$$
u=y-4x+a,\,v=by+cx+3,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v+1 \\ 9u-4v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ 9u-4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 9 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-4\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 9}[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -9 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -9 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -9 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -9 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\cdot (x-1)+1\cdot (y-3) \\ -9\cdot (x-1)+2\cdot (y-3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}y-4x+1 \\ 2y-9x+3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=y-4x+1,\,v=2y+(-9)x+3.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=1+2+(-9)=-6.
$$

questions.problem:
The affine transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=-2v-4,\,y=u+4v+6.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ of $T$ is

$$
u=2x+y+a,\,v=bx+cy-2,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2v-4 \\ u+4v+6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2v \\ u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 0-(-2)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x+4 \\ y-6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot (x+4)+1\cdot (y-6) \\ (-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (x+4)+0\cdot (y-6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x+y+2 \\ -\frac{1}{2}x-2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=2x+y+2,\,v=(-\frac{1}{2})x+0y-2.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=2+(-\frac{1}{2})+0=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Types of Images Formed by an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14045422/assets/c1ee8bc2c212708ed583c709420a856b28f6e2129c24690a504b4716b2692aa7.png)

Consider the affine transformation $T,$ given by

$$
x=u-2v+1,\,y=2u-3v+1.
$$

What would be the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any affine transformation 

$$
T:u⟶Au+b,
$$

where $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $u$ and $b$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors, we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., when $det(A)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., when $det(A)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $A$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $A$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a point on the plane.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

The given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-2v+1 \\ 2u-3v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-2v \\ 2u-3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-3)-2\cdot (-2) \\  & =1 \\  & \ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a non-singular matrix. 

Therefore, $T$ is invertible and the image of the triangle under the action of $T$ is a triangle.
